Avenue de Cortenbergh 100
Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE)

GIE is the voice of Europe's gas infrastructure operators and counts 74 members across 
Europe who develop innovative solutions to enable a climate-neutral, competitive and 
integrated energy system by 2050. Members operate transmission pipelines, underground 
storage and import terminals. They are securing and decarbonising Europe's energy 
supply by developing future-proofed solutions for transport, storage and import of 
biomethane, synthetic gasses, hydrogen and CO2.

EBA fully believes in the future potential of renewable gas in Europe. 
Founded in 2009, the association is committed to the deployment of 
sustainable biogas and biomethane production and use throughout 
the continent. EBA counts today on a well-established network of over 
380 national associations and other organisations covering the whole 
biogas and biomethane value chain across Europe and beyond.

Europe reaches a total of 1975 biomethane producing facilities by mid Q2 2026 
(see Fig.1). Compared to the previous editions of the European Biomethane Map, the 
number of plants in Europe have sharply increased (1,023 in the 2021 edition, 1,322 
in the 2022-23 edition, 1,548 in the 2023-2024 edition and 1678 in the 2025 edition) 
covering 26 countries .

At least 86% of the biomethane plants currently active in Europe are known to be 
connected to the gas grid. 7% of European biomethane plants do not have grid 
connection, and for remaining 7% of Europe’s plants no information is available in EBA 
database (see Fig. 2). Figures presented below and on the European Biomethane Map 
were originated from the EBA database. A full elaboration of the biogas and 
biomethane markets will be available in the EBA Statistical report 2026.

This map has been built with support of GIE and EBA members, who’s members have 
provided the necessary biomethane plant data. Sources for each country are listed in 
this section.
